main.why: Every batch job re-solved distribution and failures, so MapReduce lets programmers write map and reduce and leaves the rest to the framework.

main.title: Resilient Distributed Datasets: A Fault-Tolerant Abstraction for In-Memory Cluster Computing
main.why: MapReduce rereads data from disk between iterations, so Spark keeps it in memory as RDDs and rebuilds lost pieces from lineage.
Spark shuffle writes wore out the SSDs on compute hosts, so Uber moved shuffle data to a dedicated remote shuffle service.

main.title: The Log: What every software engineer should know about real-time data's unifying abstraction
main.why: Point-to-point pipelines between data systems multiply, so one ordered log of changes can feed every database, cache and data system instead.
LinkedIn needed one pipeline for huge volumes of activity data, so Kafka brokers store it as a log that consumers pull at their own pace.
Whole Kafka partitions grew too heavy to manage at LinkedIn's scale, so Northguard splits each log into small segments.
Change capture needs a table's full state and its ongoing changes, so DBLog interleaves chunked dumps with the change stream without locking the table.

main.title: The Dataflow Model
main.why: Events arrive late and out of order, so the Dataflow model handles them with windows, watermarks and triggers.

further.title: Discretized Streams: Fault-Tolerant Streaming Computation at Scale

main.title: Apache Flink: Stream and Batch Processing in a Single Engine
main.why: Separate batch and streaming engines duplicate work, so Flink runs both in one engine, treating batch as a bounded stream.

main.title: State Management in Apache Flink
main.why: Stream jobs hold state that must survive failures, so Flink injects barriers that trigger consistent checkpoints for exactly-once recovery.

background.title: Distributed Snapshots: Determining Global States of Distributed Systems

main.why: Ad events must be counted exactly once in near real time, so Uber pairs Flink checkpoints with Kafka transactions.

main.title: Dremel: Interactive Analysis of Web-Scale Datasets
main.why: Interactive queries over nested web data needed columnar storage, so Dremel encodes nested records by column, the scheme Parquet adopted.

further.title: Dremel: A Decade of Interactive SQL Analysis at Web Scale

main.title: Major Technical Advancements in Apache Hive
main.why: Hive scanned whole files, so the ORC format stores column statistics that let a query skip data its filter rules out.
Data lake storage kept growing, so Uber recompressed Parquet with ZSTD and sorted rows so they compress better.
Point lookups on a Parquet data lake meant full scans, so Spotify builds an external index that turns each lookup into one small read.

main.title: Delta Lake: High-Performance ACID Table Storage over Cloud Object Stores
main.why: Object stores cannot update many files atomically, so Delta Lake keeps a transaction log next to Parquet files for ACID tables.

further.title: Lakehouse: A New Generation of Open Platforms that Unify Data Warehousing and Advanced Analytics

main.why: Hive tables overloaded the metastore and depended on S3 listings, so Airbnb moved ingestion to Iceberg tables and Spark 3.
Rewriting whole partitions kept Uber's lake data stale, so it built Hudi to apply incremental upserts.
Notion's data is mostly updated rather than appended, which made Snowflake costly, so it built a lake on S3 with Hudi.
Each data store needed its own query tool, so Presto runs SQL across many sources through connectors.
Shared-nothing warehouses tie storage to compute, so Snowflake keeps data in S3 and runs queries on separate clusters that scale on their own.
Redshift kept its MPP engine but moved storage to S3 and added serverless, so compute scales apart from data.

main.title: Druid: A Real-time Analytical Data Store
main.why: Dashboards need fast queries on just-arrived events, so Druid serves fresh data from memory and older data from immutable column segments.

further.title: Pinot: Realtime OLAP for 530 Million Users

main.title: ClickHouse: Lightning Fast Analytics for Everyone
main.why: Real-time analytics needs fast inserts and fast scans, so ClickHouse writes sorted parts, merges them in the background and runs vectorized queries.
